spans.s:
To loose, set free, release, let go, let loose, liberate, deliver (from
 captivity &c.); वनाय … यशोधनो धेनुमृषेर्मुमोच

‘let not thy limbs droop’,
 ‘do not despond’.
To set free, loosen (as the voice); कण्ठं मुञ्चति बर्हिणः समदनः
‘loosens his throat or voice’ i. e. raises a cry.

To leave, abandon, quit, give up, lay aside, relinquish; रात्रिर्गता
 मतिमतां वर मुञ्च शग्याम्
To set apart, take away, except. See मुक्त्वा.
To cast, throw, hurl, fling, discharge; मृगेषु शरान् मुमुक्षोः

To emit, drop, pour forth or down, shed, let fall (tears &c.); अपसृतपाण्डुपत्रा
 मुञ्चन्त्यश्रूणीव लताः Ś. 4. 12; चिरविरहजं मुञ्चतो बाष्पमुष्णम्

To be loosed or released, be freed or absolved from (with abl. or instr.);
 मुच्यते सर्वपापेभ्यः &c.
To abandon, deviate or swerve from. ━Caus. (मोचयति-ते)
To cause to be freed or liberated.
To loose, set at liberty, liberate.
To wish to free or liberate &c.
(मुमुक्षते, मोक्षते) To long for final emancipation.

I. €1 Ā. (मोचते) To deceive, cheat; see मुञ्च्.
━II. €6 U. (मुञ्चति-ते, मुमोच-मुमुचे, अमुचत्-अमुक्त, मोक्ष्यति-ते, मोक्तुम्, मुक्त)

N. of an ancient king, son of Māndhātṛ. [For having assisted the
 gods in their wars with the demons he got, as a reward, the boon of long
 and unbroken sleep. The gods also decreed that whosoever dared to interrupt
 his sleep should be burnt to ashes. When Kṛṣṇa wanted to kill the
 mighty Kālayavana, he cunningly decoyed him to the cave of Muchakunda,
 and on his entering it, he was burnt down by the fire which emanated from
 the kingʼs eye.]
.━{@Comp.@}: मुचकुन्दप्रसादकः

.━{@Comp.@}: मुचकुन्दप्रसादकः
